To cut a release, push a git tag named `vYYYY.MM.N`. For example, `v2026.09.2` is the third-numbered tag format in September 2026. `N` is the release number within that month. This comes from a project convention stored in EngramDB.

1. Choose the tag for the current month. Today is 2026-10-01, so the next one would be `v2026.10.N`. Check `git tag` for existing tags this month before picking `N`.
2. Tag the commit on `main` and push the tag. For example, `git tag v2026.10.1 && git push origin v2026.10.1`.
3. Let CI build and publish. Don't publish by hand.

I didn't find a release script or doc in the repo. The only other file that matched my search was `scripts/export.py`, and it only matched on the words "release" or "tag". The convention may not cover every step, such as changelog updates, version bumps or pre-release checks. If your team has those, they aren't recorded here.
